بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ.

سُورَةُ التَّكْوِيرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾

اخْتَلَفَ في مَعْنى ”كُوِّرَتْ“ هُنا أكْثَرُ مِن عَشَرَةِ أقْوالٍ، وكُلُّها تَدُورُ عَلى نِهايَةِ أمْرِها.

فَقِيلَ: ”كُوِّرَتْ“: لُفَّ بَعْضُها عَلى بَعْضٍ، فانْطَمَسَ نُورُها.

وَقِيلَ: حُجِبَتْ بِكارَةٍ، أيْ: لُفَّتْ بِها. وقِيلَ: أُلْقِيَتْ في البَحْرِ. وقِيلَ: دَخَلَتْ في العَرْشِ. وقِيلَ: اضْمَحَلَّتْ. وقِيلَ: نُكِّسَتْ. وقالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: نَقُولُ كَما قالَ اللَّهُ تَعالى: ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾.

وَالَّذِي يَشْهَدُ لَهُ القُرْآنُ، أنَّ هَذا كُلَّهُ راجِعٌ إلى تَغَيُّرِ حالِها في آخِرِ أمْرِها؛ لِأنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى جَعَلَ لَها أجَلًا مُسَمًّى، ومَعْنى ذَلِكَ أنَّها تَنْتَهِي إلَيْهِ عَلى الوَجْهِ الَّذِي يَعْلَمُهُ - سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى - كَما في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ [لقمان: ٢٩].

فَمَفْهُومُهُ: أنَّهُ إذا جاءَ هَذا الأجَلُ تَوَقَّفَتْ عَنْ جَرَيانِها.

وَهُوَ ما يُشِيرُ إلَيْها قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا بَرِقَ البَصَرُ﴾ ﴿وَخَسَفَ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ﴾ [القيامة: ٧ - ٩]، أيْ: بَعْدَ أنْ لَمْ يَجْتَمِعا قَطُّ، وما كانَ لَهُما أنْ يَجْتَمِعا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ، كَما في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَها أنْ تُدْرِكَ القَمَرَ ولا اللَّيْلُ سابِقُ النَّهارِ وكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [يس: ٤٠] (p-٤٣٨)

وَلَعَلَّ أقْرَبَ الأقْوالِ المَنقُولَةِ في ذَلِكَ هو القَوْلُ بِأنَّهُ بِمَعْنى: نُكِّسَتْ. أيْ: رُدَّتْ إلى حَيْثُ أتَتْ، كَما في الحَدِيثِ، فَتَطْلُعُ مِن مَغْرِبِها، وعَلَيْهِ فَتَجْتَمِعُ مَعَ القَمَرِ.

Allah's statement: ﴿And when the stars fall, dispersing﴾.

It has been said: "inkadarat" means they pour down (or are scattered). It has also been said: they change from "kudra" (dimness, turbidity). All of these meanings are interrelated and there is no contradiction among them.

The first meaning is supported by Allah's statement: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾ [al-Infitar: 2].

The second meaning is supported by: ﴿And when the stars are obliterated﴾ [al-Mursalat: 8], because when they are scattered and leave their places, and their order is disturbed, their light has gone and they have been obliterated.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾

That is: He takes them away from their place.

Earlier, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, explained the condition of the mountains at the end of this world in several passages. Among the most important of these is at His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blast﴾ [Ta-Ha: 105], and at His saying, exalted is He, in Surah al-Kahf: ﴿And the day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth laid bare﴾ [al-Kahf: 47].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾ ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾. Al-wa'd (burying alive) means heaviness, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the preserving of them does not burden Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

Al-maww'udah (the buried one) is the one weighed down with dirt until death. She was a girl who was buried alive: they would dig a pit for her, throw her into it, and then pour dirt over her.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for what sin she was killed﴾ indicates that she had no sin for which she should be killed; rather, the crime lies upon her killer.

However, because of the enormity of the crime, the question is directed at her as a rebuke to the one who buried her.

It has been reported from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, his saying: "There were two matters in the Jahiliyyah. One of them makes me weep and the other makes me laugh."

As for what makes me weep: I took a daughter of mine to bury her. I was digging the pit for her, and she was shaking the dirt off my beard, while she did not know what I intended for her. Whenever I remember that, I weep.

As for the other: I used to make a god from dates, placing it near my head to guard me at night. When I rose in the morning in good health, I would eat it. Whenever I remember that, I laugh at myself.

As for the cause of their undertaking this atrocious crime and what drove them to commit it, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, discussed it extensively at his saying, exalted is He, in Surah "al-Nahl": ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters—glory be to Him—while for themselves they have what they desire.﴾ ﴿And when one of them is given good tidings of a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.﴾ ﴿He hides himself from the people because of the evil of that of which he has been given tidings. Should he keep it despite disgrace or bury it in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.﴾ [al-Nahl: 57–59, as cited] — the verse.

* *

On this occasion, there are two warnings that must be mentioned.

The first warning: what resembles burying (al-wa'd) in these modern times, namely, resorting to preventing pregnancy by any means whatsoever.

I have studied this matter in the past and present. In the past, it concerned the practice of 'azl (coitus interruptus). A hadith of Jabir concerning it says: "We used to practice 'azl while the Qur'an was being revealed." Narrated by Muslim.

Ishaq added: Sufyan said: "If it were something forbidden, the Qur'an would have forbidden it to us." It also includes: "This reached the Prophet ﷺ and he did not forbid us."

Strong warning also came in the hadith of Judamah bint Wahb, sister of 'Ukashah, who said: "I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among people, and he said: 'I had intended to forbid ghilah (nursing during pregnancy), but I looked at the Romans and Persians and found that they practice ghilah, and it does not harm their children at all.' They asked him about 'azl, and he said: 'That is the hidden burial (al-wa'd al-khafi).'"

'Abd Allah added in his narration from al-Muqri' an addition, which is: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾.

In the first hadith there is what indicates approval (al-taqrir), and in the second there is what indicates strong disapproval.

Also in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Sa'id: "We fought with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, and we took captive some of the noblest of the Arabs. The period of abstinence grew long for us, and we desired ransom, so we wished to enjoy them and practice 'azl. We said: 'Shall we do that while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us and we do not ask him?' So we asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'There is no harm upon you that you not do it; for every soul that is to exist until the Day of Resurrection will exist.'"

In another narration: "Indeed Allah has written who will be creating until the Day of Resurrection."

In another narration: "He said to us: 'And indeed you do it, and indeed you do it, and indeed you do it. There is no soul that is to exist until the Day of Resurrection except that it will exist.'"

In another narration: "There is no harm upon you that you not do it; for it is only destiny (al-qadar)."

Abu Muhammad said: His saying "There is no harm upon you" is closer to prohibition.

Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, it is as if this is a rebuke."

You see that his saying ﷺ "And indeed you do it" indicates his lack of prior knowledge, which conflicts with the addition in the hadith of Jabir: "This reached the Prophet ﷺ and he did not forbid us." We keep the saying of Jabir, which those who permit it cite as evidence, and it is opposed by: "that which is buried" (al-mawudah) or "the hidden burial" (al-wa'd al-khafi).

The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah had two causes for burying (al-wa'd):

The first: economic, fear of poverty, and poverty that is present.

The second: zealous pride and jealousy.

The Qur'an refuted them concerning the first cause in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.﴾ [al-Isra': 31].

And His saying: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them﴾ [al-An'am: 151].

Finally, this questioning was a severe rebuke to them: ﴿When the buried infant girl is asked﴾ (p-441)

In this verse the matter was raised again, in a different form, which the enemies of the Muslims raised as a deception for the naive, so it was raised from the economic side.

Its well-known origin among writers of this age is the theory of "Malthus," and now for a military purpose: to reduce the number of Muslim soldiers, when the enemy learned that Islam permits polygyny, two, three, and four wives, so they wished to halt this growth.

It suffices here to cite his saying ﷺ: "Marry, and multiply, for I will boast of you before the nations." In another narration: "I will outnumber the nations through you." And in it: "Marry the loving, fertile woman," and similar.

I had compiled a research paper on this in a comprehensive lecture for this purpose, from the perspective of politics and economics, and in defense, along with statistics of countries that demand this practice, which refutes the view of everyone who holds it.

What concerns us in this context is alerting the Muslims that this call to limit or regulate population growth originates with the Jews, and its promotion in the East is from Western states, and many Western states spend vast wealth to spread this matter in the states of the Middle East, especially the Islamic and Arab ones.

The second warning: concerning what the advocates of women's liberation declare under the guise of supporting them, while in reality they are the promoters of their misery, hostile to them, and demolishing what Allah has granted them under the shade of Islam.

For in the Jahiliyyah, women were in this state among their conditions: they were buried alive, inherited like goods, their personhood neglected, and other things. Islam granted them what establishes their personhood from the outset, by giving them their right to life like men, then their choice in marriage, their right to inheritance, and more.

This has been discussed at length in several places, among them the Shaykh's, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, commentary at his saying, exalted is He: ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 34].

(p-442) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Hellfire is set ablaze﴾

The explanation of this meaning was already given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, when discussing His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat al-Hajj: ﴿And among mankind is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾ ﴿It is decreed for him that whoever allies with him, he will lead him astray and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Paradise is brought near﴾

Zulfa (al-zulfa) means nearness (al-qurba), and "uzlifat" means "qurribat" (was brought near). The explanation of this was already given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, in Surah Qaf, at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, not far off﴾ [Qaf: 31].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul will know what it has brought forward﴾

The word "soul" (nafs) here is meant in a general sense, i.e., every soul, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [before it]﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 30].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 15:**

Allah's words: ﴿So I swear by the stars that recede﴾ ﴿that run and hide﴾ ﴿and by the night when it departs﴾ ﴿and by the morning when it breathes﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger﴾

The apparent meaning of His words ﴿So I do not swear﴾ is a negation of an oath, but it is certainly an oath, as evidenced by the explicit statement of the answer to the oath in His words ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger﴾ [At-Takwir: 19].

By this, what preceded at the beginning of the surah "Al-Qiyamah" is preferred: ﴿I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 1].

The same applies to what comes later: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾ [Al-Balad: 1].

Note.

The exegetes agree that Allah may swear by whatever He wills of His creation, because they indicate His power, and it is not permissible for a created being to swear except by Allah, the Exalted.

But: is there an intended meaning in the variation of what Allah swears by, or is it merely for mentioning and multiplicity of what is sworn by?

(p-443) After reflection, it became clear, and Allah knows best, that He, glorified is He, does not swear by a thing in one place rather than another except for a purpose related to that place, where there is a relevance and connection between what is sworn by and what is sworn to. This may appear clearly, and it may be hidden.

This is indeed what wisdom and the inimitability of the Qur'an require, although I have not come across a study on it.

However, among what points to this subject is what came with an oath concerning Makkah twice, in two different situations.

The first: His words ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾ ﴿while you are a resident of this city﴾ ﴿and by the begetter and what he begot﴾ ﴿We have certainly created man in toil﴾ [Al-Balad: 1-4].

The second place: His words ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinai﴾ ﴿and this secure city﴾ ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [At-Tin: 1-4].

In both places, what is sworn by is Makkah the Honored, and what is sworn to in both places is the creation of man. But in the first place, what is sworn to is the struggle of man from his first birth, to his upbringing, to his toil in life, to his end and death.

Among that is the struggle of the Prophet (ﷺ) from his birth until his father died before him, and his mother joined him while he was in his childhood. After the revelation, he struggled with his people and encountered from them severe harm, until they plotted to kill him. It is as if He says to him: be patient with that, for the struggle is inevitable, and it is inherent in man just as your attachment to this city since your birth.

In the mention of ﴿and the begetter and what he begot﴾ there is an indication of the beginning of the struggle and its intensity from the state of birth and the nature of childhood. For this reason he mentioned this city here without any description.

As for the second place: the thing sworn to, although it is the creation of man, is in the best of stature, and this is the greatest blessing upon him. He brought what is sworn by as a reference to the blessings and their multiplicity: the fig and the olive, whether what is meant by them is the fruit mentioned or their places, which is Jerusalem together with Mount Sinai.

(p-444) So He also mentioned Makkah, but with a fitting description, saying: ﴿and this secure city﴾. It is as if He says: whoever bestowed upon those lands goodness, blessing and sanctity, bestowed upon man the blessing of the goodness of his form, the goodness of his constitution, and his excellence over the rest of His creatures. And Allah knows best.

Here He swears by the states of the stars according to the most correct opinions, in their appearing, their disappearing and their movement; and by ﴿the night when it departs﴾: it comes and goes, or it lights up and darkens; ﴿and the morning when it breathes﴾: i.e., it appears and shines. These are two effects of the sun's effects in its setting and its rising.

And what is sworn to is that the Qur'an is the word of a noble Messenger. It is as if He says: the Qur'an that is sworn to, its state in steadfastness and manifestation, and the state of people with it, is like the state of these stars that are fixed for you, in their appearing at times and their disappearing at others.

And like the state of the night and the morning: it is for some people a place of trust and guidance, like the morning in its brightness; their hearts are open to it and their minds are guided by it; it is for them a spirit and a light. And for other people their hearts are dark before it, their insights are blind to it, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness upon them. And some people are at times and at times like the stars at some moments and at others: at times its light flashes in their hearts, so its landmarks appear and they walk with it; and at times its light is absent from them, so their minds withdraw from it and their hearts hide behind it, as Allah said about them: ﴿Whenever it lights up for them they walk in it, and when it darkens over them they stand still﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 20].

It is not far-fetched to say that, from another aspect, the stars are considered like the previous scriptures: their appearance passed in their time and their concealment after it.

﴿and by the night when it departs﴾: it is the darkness of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance).

﴿and by the morning when it breathes﴾: it corresponds to the manifestation of Islam, and that it will spread like the spread of daylight; no power has ever been able to veil it, and it will encompass all the horizons, however much they stand against it: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [As-Saff: 8].

It may be that this proposal is strange to some people, especially since I have not come across an independent study on it, nor a direction that points to it. But with investigation I found its consistency in multiple places, and it is worthy of being devoted to a treatise.

(p-445) Among what this direction has been consistent in is the surah "Ad-Duha". Allah says: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾ ﴿Your Lord has not bidden you farewell, nor has He detested you﴾ [Ad-Duha: 1-3]. The thing sworn to is the non-abandonment of him (ﷺ) and not being forsaken by Him. So He brought as what is sworn by the two divisions of time, night and day, as if He says to him: your Lord has not detested you, nor has He forsaken you, neither in the brightness of the day when you go forth for your striving, nor in the darkness of the night when you retire to your house.

It is well known what his uncle Abu Talib did when he used to have him sleep with his children at night; when all had taken their beds, he would secretly come and lift him from his place and place one of his children in his position, even if someone intended him harm. Then, seeing him in his first place, he would find his son there instead, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would be safe.

As for His words ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [Ad-Duha: 4], i.e., better than everything the sun has risen upon and the night has covered.

From it also, and more clearly so, is the surah "Al-Asr". Allah says: ﴿By time﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿except those who have believed﴾ [Al-Asr: 1-3], to the end of the surah. The thing sworn to is the state of man, which is predominantly loss, except for those whom Allah the Exalted excepted. So what is sworn by is "time" (al-asr), which is contemporaneous with man throughout his life and is the place of his action, by which he loses and profits. It is contemporaneous with him and is the most truthful witness against him.

I had heard from the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, saying: life and the span of existence are a proof against man, like the Message and the warning alike. He mentioned His words: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would be mindful could be mindful therein, and the warner came to you?﴾ [Fatir: 37]. So in the verse He made ta'mir (granting a long life), which is the occupation of a lifespan, a cause for remembrance and reflection, and a respite for action, just as you inform a person of a matter and then give him respite until he does what has passed before him; so it is more effective as proof against him.

Thus the oath in "Al-Asr" was upon profit and loss, the most fitting connection between them, since man's life has been made like a standing marketplace, in which the commodity is action and the one who trades is man, as Allah said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a commerce that will save you from a painful punishment? ﴾ ﴿You believe in Allah﴾ [As-Saff: 10-11].

In the authentic hadith in Muslim: "Glory be to Allah fills the scale," and in it: "Every person goes out in the morning, selling his soul, either freeing it or destroying it." So if he occupies his lifespan in good, he has profited and freed himself; otherwise he has lost and destroyed it.

Allah's words also point to this: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111].

Thus it is established that the world is a marketplace, the commodity in it is the action of man, and the dealing in it is with Allah, the Exalted. So the connection and relevance with what is sworn by and what is sworn to became manifest.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 81, verse 19:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.﴾

They agree that the "word" (qawl) refers to the Qur'an. As for the "noble messenger," it refers to Jibril (Gabriel) (peace be upon him), as evidenced by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Possessed of power, with standing before the Lord of the Throne, obeyed there and trustworthy. And your companion is not mad.﴾ [At-Takwir: 22].

So "your companion" here is Muhammad (ﷺ), who has been in their company since his birth. And the one "possessed of power, with standing before the Lord of the Throne" is Jibril (peace be upon him). Attributing the word to him may raise the doubt that the word is from him, although it is the speech of Allah, exalted is He.

The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on us and on him, answered this in order to remove the appearance of contradiction, by citing explicit texts that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, exalted is He. He said: "Within this very verse there is what refutes this doubt and establishes that truth, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿it is the word of a messenger.﴾ For a messenger does not bring a word from himself. Rather, the word he brings is what he was sent with from another, to those to whom he was sent with it."

**Note on describing Jibril (peace be upon him) with these attributes:**

It is a clear text on his being entrusted with preserving what he was sent with and on its protection from alteration and substitution. Because he is "with standing" (makin), nothing reaches him that would disrupt his message, and because he is "obeyed there" (muta') and "trustworthy" (amin), other beings do not influence him, and the trustworthy one does not betray or substitute. Thus the Qur'an he brought was safeguarded both from anyone gaining power over it to change it and from the one who brought it changing it. All of this serves as an explanation of the chain of transmission (sanad) for receiving the noble Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿And your companion is not mad﴾ is a clarification of the completion of the chain, where He said: ﴿And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon. And he is not stingy with the unseen.﴾ [At-Takwir: 23–24]. Thus He negated from him (ﷺ) any deficiency in receiving the revelation by negating the defect of madness. He is in perfection of intellect and strength of perception. Earlier, He affirmed for him the perfection of character: ﴿And indeed you are of exalted character.﴾ [Al-Qalam: 4].

He also affirmed for him the meeting (luqya) with Jibril, so Jibril was not confused for him with anyone else. This is the highest level of the chain. Thus there was gathered for him (ﷺ) moral perfection (al-kamal al-khuluqi) and physical perfection (al-kamal al-khilqi), with the kha' pronounced with a damma or a kasra, meaning perfection in both the sensory and the meaningful sense. Then He negated from him the accusation that he would withhold anything of what he was sent with, despite its preciousness, the loftiness of its status, and the grandeur of its sciences, and that it is the speech of the Lord of the worlds.

At the conclusion, there is an indication to them that it is not: ﴿the word of an accursed devil﴾ [At-Takwir: 25], since He had previously said: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 212], and: ﴿whoever listens now will find a watching flame lying in wait for him.﴾ [Al-Jinn: 9]. Therefore there remains for them no reason to turn away from it. They are obligated to take it, since it has become established that it is the speech of Allah, brought by a noble messenger and conveyed to your companion, the possessor of exalted character, and it is not the word of an accursed devil.

So they are obligated to take it, otherwise where will you go? Where will you turn away from it, after its chain and its source have been established for you?

A parallel to this chain, in glorifying the Qur'an and establishing that it comes from Allah, is His saying at the beginning of Surah An-Najm: ﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred. Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed. Taught him by one mighty in power, possessor of strength; he stood firm, while he was on the highest horizon.﴾ [An-Najm: 2, 3–7].

(p-434) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Takwir

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger.﴾

The apparent meaning of this verse may lead the ignorant to imagine that the Qur'an is the speech of Jibril, although the Qur'anic verses explicitly state many times that it is the speech of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿...so grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah﴾ and His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses are made precise, then explained in detail, from One who is Wise and Acquainted.﴾ [11].

The answer is clear from the verse itself: the appearance of the statement ﴿Indeed, it is the word of﴾ is removed by the mention of the messenger, for it indicates that the speech belongs to another, but he was sent to convey it. So the meaning of His saying ﴿the word of a messenger﴾ is his conveying it from the One who sent him, without addition or subtraction.

Allah's statement: ﴿Where, then, are you going?﴾ is like one who blocks their path except toward Him, because the Qur'an, in its descent from Allah upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), contains no doubt (shubhah) or accusation (tuhmah) whatsoever. Thus it is not for the intelligent person to turn away from it, and every going toward anything else is a blocked path, misguidance, and ruin.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿for whoever among you wills to take the straight path﴾. That is: after this clarification, the strength of this evidence, and the manifestation of the establishment of the Message, the one who warns has fulfilled his duty of warning. ﴿For whoever among you wills to take the straight path﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds.﴾

In it is the matter of predestination (qadar) and of the universal will (al-irada al-kawniyya) and the predestinarian will (al-qadariyya). The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, discussed it in several places. Among them is in Surah "al-Zukhruf" at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 20], and in it is the debate of the Mu'tazili with the Sunni.

And among them is in Surah "al-Dhariyat": ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.﴾ ﴿I do not want from them any provision﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56-57], and the difference between the universal will and the predestinarian will.

Note.

Although many people cite this verse in the matter of qada' and qadar, its importance on the side of constant supplication to Allah should not be overlooked, by seeking Allah's favour upon us in being granted steadfastness as a bounty from Him, just as He commanded us in the prayer, in every rak'ah of it, to ask Him this request: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatiha: 6].

Another note.

Steadfastness has been mentioned in general terms here, and it is alluded to in Surah "al-Fatiha": "the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour," as is known. And Allah knows best.
